title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-27
content:
TL;DR: sudden ~30% drop in tail throughput on staging clusters between 2025-11-08 and 2025-11-11. Root cause likely a misconfiguration in continuous-batching heuristics combined with a recent KV-cache change. Repro + commands below, plus hypotheses and next steps.

Symptoms:
- Client-visible p95 throughput dropped from ~850 reqs/s -> ~600 reqs/s for gen-small model (gpt-small-v1) on staging-dedicated-1.
- Latency p95 increased ~1.4x, p50 neutral. Suggests batching/build-up problem causing backpressure.
- Regression appeared after deploy 2025-11-09 of patch that touched kv-cache eviction and batching policy (PR #462).

First repro (quick):
1) Run load test against staging-dedicated-1 with identical query distribution used in canary: short prompts (avg 40 tokens), bursty arrival (Poisson with lambda=800).
2) Observe throughput drop and latency spikes.

Key commands I ran locally on staging cluster (notes + outputs trimmed):
- tail logs: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runtime --since=2h | grep "batching" | tail -n 200
  -> many lines with: "batch_create_delay_ms=15" and occasional warnings: "batcher: dropped request due to build timeout"

- curl metrics endpoint: curl -s http://staging-dedicated-1:9100/metrics | grep continuous_batcher
  -> continuous_batcher_queue_length 12
     continuous_batcher_avg_build_time_ms 42.3
     continuous_batcher_max_build_time_ms 1204.0
     continuous_batcher_builds 3240

- Inspect KV-cache metrics: curl -s http://staging-dedicated-1:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache
  -> kv_cache_hit_rate 0.61 (was ~0.78 before)
     kv_cache_evictions 1345
     kv_cache_avg_lookup_ms 0.8

- Hotfix attempt (reverted batching policy flag): kubectl -n redwood patch deploy serving-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ci.hotfix":"batch-window-revert-20251110"}}}}}'
  -> small improvement but not full recovery; p95 moved to ~720 reqs/s

Logs/Errors seen (snippets):
- "batcher: build timed out after 50ms, returning partial batch (size=4, expected=16)"
- "request queue grew beyond target, applying backpressure"
- "kv-cache miss; falling back to full decode path"

Observations and timeline:
- 2025-11-08: baseline stable (monitoring shows healthy batching: avg_build_time ~12ms, queue_length 2-4).
- 2025-11-09: deploy PR #462 (kv-cache eviction/refactor + small change to continuous-batching heuristic: prefer_min_batch_time increased from 10ms -> 15ms).
- 2025-11-09 late: small p50 latency regressions observed in canary but not escalated.
- 2025-11-10: p95 throughput degradation begins, KV cache hit rate drops.
- 2025-11-11: full staging alert fired.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Mis-tuned batching heuristic: increasing prefer_min_batch_time caused more waiting for batches to assemble, but because KV-cache hit rate dropped we now have more expensive per-request path, causing batches to take longer to finish and backing up the queue -> lower throughput and higher p95. Evidence: build_time jumped, and messages about partial batches/timeouts.
2) KV-cache refactor introduced an additional synchronous lookup in the hot path on misses, increasing per-request processing time and amplifying batching effects. Evidence: kv_cache_avg_lookup_ms unchanged but evictions and hit_rate changed; logs show "kv-cache miss; falling back to full decode path" more frequently.
3) Regression in priority routing (requests with small token lengths getting deprioritized into larger prefetched batches), interaction with batching policy. Less likely but possible given recent routing changes in same PR set.
4) Resource contention (CPU/GPU) causing increase in processing time. Checked node CPU and GPU utilization; GPU saturated sometimes but not correlated with deploy time.

Quick experiments run so far (results):
- Reverted prefer_min_batch_time to 10ms on a single canary replica: partial recovery in p95 but still below baseline. Conclusion: batching param mattered but not full story.
- Disabled KV-cache eviction changes (roll back PR changes to eviction heuristic) on canary: combined with revert of batching param -> throughput back to ~940 reqs/s (near baseline). Strong signal that both changes interact.
- Forced batch size limit to 8 (was 16) for test: increased throughput slightly but p95 still noisy -> suggests larger batches were sometimes failing to fill in time.

Things to investigate deeper / next steps:
- Reproduce locally with controlled kv-cache hit/miss injection to measure impact of miss path on batch build/finish times. (TODO: add flag to runtime to force kv-cache miss for X% of requests).
- Add more granular tracing for batch lifecycle: timestamp per stage (enqueue, build_start, build_end, dispatch, finish). We already have partial traces but need sub-ms resolution.
- Run ablation: revert kv-cache refactor fully on staging and run full load test for 2h. If recovers, schedule revert in prod.
- Evaluate reducing prefer_min_batch_time back to 8-10ms and lowering max_build_time threshold. Add dynamic tuning based on observed kv-cache hit rate.
- Add synthetic telemetry: record batch success ratio (full vs partial) by model and token length to detect patterns.

Short-term mitigation options (safe):
- Rollback kv-cache eviction refactor (low-risk for short term).
- Reduce prefer_min_batch_time to 8ms cluster-wide for staging and Dedicated for affected customers.
- Increase batch build timeout threshold to avoid frequent partial batches if doing so doesn't increase latency too much.

Notes to self:
- Talk to Priya about the eviction threshold change (she authored that part).
- Ask infra to give me 24h historical pod-level CPU/GPU traces for the canary window 2025-11-08 -> 2025-11-12.
- Put together a small reproducible harness that toggles kv-cache hits and batching params; aim to finish by 2025-12-02.

Hypothesis tester checklist (for next run):
- [ ] Synthetic load with forced KV hits only -> expect throughput stable; if not, batching alone still broken.
- [ ] Synthetic load with forced KV misses only -> expect build_time increase; observe p95 impact.
- [ ] Experiment matrix: prefer_min_batch_time {6,10,15} x max_batch_size {8,12,16} x kv_cache_hit_rate {0.9,0.7,0.5}

Misc notes:
- Related historical doc: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-13 had earlier notes about prefer_min_batch_time tuning during Q2 2025; check for lessons.
- Keep INF-897 updated with findings; prioritize rollback if we see consistent recovery after reverting kv-cache changes.

End of scratchpad.
